key_insight: A graph neural network trained on smaller GW calculations predicts quasiparticle energy levels in large supercells at a fraction of the computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The approach could make accurate electronic-structure calculations more practical for defects, surfaces, and moiré systems where direct GW calculations become prohibitive.
method: Represent atomic positions as graph nodes and atom-to-atom distances as edges.
Use DFT wavefunction projections onto localized atomic orbitals as model features.
Build a targeted, compact GW training dataset and tune hyperparameters with Bayesian optimization.
evidence_signal: For monolayer MoS₂ with a sulfur vacancy, the abstract reports mean absolute errors of 10–50 meV for predicted quasiparticle energy levels.
watch_item: Accuracy beyond the demonstrated MoS₂ defect system remains to be established, and deployment still requires DFT-derived features and representative GW training data.
paper_title: Graph Neural Networks for Accurate Quasiparticle Energy Levels in Large Supercells of Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
